headline: Caltech's Physics AI ditches Transformers for Neural Operators, ingesting 5 trillion data points
summary: A new company, Accelerated Understanding Inc., founded by Caltech researchers, uses neural operators to process 5 trillion data points in a single prompt, a million times more than current frontier models.
details: Caltech researchers Anima Anandkumar and Benedikt Jenik have founded Accelerated Understanding Inc., moving beyond traditional Transformer architectures. Their new approach utilizes neural operators, a fundamentally different method for AI systems to represent and process data.

Unlike token-by-token attention in Transformers, neural operators handle problems in continuous space, learning mappings between functions. This allows their system to ingest an unprecedented 5 trillion data points in a single prompt, vastly outperforming models like Anthropic's Claude or Google's Gemini.

Marketed as "enterprise physics AI," the company targets domains such as oil & gas, materials science, and industrial optimization. Neural operators are designed to process massive datasets of continuous measurements and produce physically plausible results, avoiding the hallucination issues common with text-trained Transformers.

This development marks a significant architectural fork in the road for the AI industry, which has largely focused on scaling Transformers for the past four years. While other labs optimize existing architectures, Anandkumar and Jenik are exploring a completely different foundation.

Anandkumar, formerly head of NVIDIA's AI research group, brings significant credibility to this venture, alongside mathematician Jenik. Their bet is rooted in the mathematical properties of operator learning, which can solve specific problem classes at scales and efficiencies beyond Transformer capabilities.

The timing is notable as frontier labs face challenges with reasoning benchmarks and inference efficiency, prompting a re-evaluation of AI architectures. Accelerated Understanding Inc. proposes abandoning the Transformer structure entirely for a specific segment of the market.

This technology won't compete with general chat models like ChatGPT or Claude. Instead, it aims to provide sophisticated, physics-heavy enterprises with solutions for differential equations and fluid dynamics, integrating into existing physics and engineering budgets.

The emergence of neural operators raises questions about the future of Transformer dominance. It suggests a potential shift towards hybrid AI stacks, where different architectural substrates are optimized for distinct tasks, moving away from the idea of a single universal foundation model.

headline: Duck.ai offers free GPT & Claude chat with no signup or card
summary: Duck.ai by DuckDuckGo provides free access to popular AI models like GPT and Claude, ensuring user privacy with anonymized requests and no stored chats.
details: Duck.ai, a new service from DuckDuckGo, now allows users to chat with several leading AI models, including GPT and Claude, completely free of charge. This platform is designed for privacy-conscious users who want quick access without the need for sign-ups or credit card details.

A core feature of Duck.ai is its commitment to user privacy. All user requests are anonymized, and chat conversations are not stored on DuckDuckGo's servers by default, offering a secure environment for AI interactions.

The service aims to provide a convenient and private alternative for engaging with powerful language models. It eliminates common barriers like account creation, making advanced AI accessible to a broader audience instantly.

Additionally, Duck.ai includes a "Templates" feature, enabling users to quickly answer frequently asked questions or store reusable snippets. This enhances productivity for regular users, streamlining their interactions with the AI models.
